title: Regression hunt index and sift workflow for benchmark anomalies
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Create a repeatable, operational workflow and storage/indexing pattern for discovering, hunting, and remediating performance regressions surfaced by our benchmark harness (tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, error rates). This ticket designs the 'Regression Hunt Index' (RHI) and the 'Sift' triage flow: a structured data model and an interactive comparison UI that lets engineers quickly group correlated anomalies, reproduce them in a canary harness, and link remediation artifacts (PRs, rollbacks, infra tickets).
acceptance_criteria: A persisted RHI schema that links benchmark runs to model artifact id, runtime config (batch size, quantization profile), hardware fingerprint, and KV-cache metrics
Comparison UI view that can diff two runs and surface metric deltas (tokens/sec, p95, p99, error-rate) with visual heatmaps and change attribution
Triage workflow documented in the UI: mark as 'spurious', 'needs-reproduce', 'candidate-bug', or 'rollout-blocker' and attach evidence (trace links, kernel logs, PRs)
Playbook steps to reproduce in a canary harness and automated rerun job template that captures full trace and kernel selection logs
Retention and dedupe policy implemented for RHI results (30d hot, 365d cold) and an archival S3 path pattern
End-to-end integration test that injects a synthetic regression and verifies detection -> triage -> assign -> reproduce flows
steps: Design storage keys for RHI: (model_id, model_version, runtime_commit, hw_region, batch_profile, seq_len_bucket, run_timestamp)
Define anomaly score: weighted combination of p95 delta, tokens/sec decline, error-rate increase, and kv-cache-hit delta
Implement ingestion pipeline: benchmark harness POSTs normalized result to ingest-api which writes to RHI (DynamoDB) + raw artifacts to S3
Build compare UI widget that overlays two runs and shows per-shard latencies, kernel selection diff, and sample request replay links
Write canary repro job (k8s CronJob template) that replays failing requests with identical seed and records traces
Document triage playbook and add canned Slack escalation messages and oncall runbook links
decision_log: 2025-11-14: Chose DynamoDB for RHI primary index to support quick query by (model_version, runtime_commit) and TTL-based expiry. Considered Postgres but rejected for scale and write patterns.
2025-11-17: Anomaly score formula agreed: 0.5*normalized(p95_delta) + 0.3*normalized(tokens_per_sec_drop) + 0.15*error_rate_increase + 0.05*kv_cache_miss_delta. Tuned after historic incident replay.
2025-11-20: UI will emphasize 'repro run' vs 'production snapshot' instead of raw diffs to reduce noise for non-engineer stakeholders.
2025-11-22: We will store raw kernel-selection logs only for runs with anomaly_score > 0.6 to control storage costs.
updates: 2025-11-12: Ticket created after incident IR-2025-11-09 showed a subtle regressions where quantized kernels reduced tokens/sec by 12% for seq_len>2048.
2025-11-15: Proto schema implemented in branch feat/rhi-schema. Ingest endpoint demoed to reliability team. Feedback: include sequence_length_histogram in primary index.
2025-11-18: UX session with PM/Design. Decided to add an 'explain' column that surfaces likely root cause (kernel, batch-size, infra) using simple heuristics.
2025-11-21: Infra approved DynamoDB table and S3 lifecycle policy. Created infra ticket INF-8902 to provision encryption keys and bucket.
2025-11-25: First end-to-end smoke run with synthetic regression succeeded. Comparison UI now shows per-step waterfall and sample request replay. Working on tests and accessibility fixes.
notes: Trade-offs: Storing full per-token traces for every run is prohibitively expensive; prefer lightweight fingerprints plus raw dumps for flagged runs.
Correlation: We should correlate RHI anomalies with deployment events (git commits, canary flips) and capacity events (GPU maintenance windows).
Mitigation pattern: auto-create a rollback candidate PR template with observed delta metrics and suggested revert commit when anomaly_score > 0.85 and customer_impact=high.
Operational: add a scheduled job to re-score historical runs after any change to anomaly_score formula and alert on re-classifications.
risks: False positives from noisy workloads could create alert fatigue; mitigation: gating alerts behind anomaly_score threshold and business-logic filters
Storage costs could grow if thresholds too low; mitigation: aggressive retention + sampled trace captures
Reproducibility: non-deterministic kernels may make canary repro unsuccessful; mitigation: capture kernel seed and deterministic flags in run metadata
next_steps: Finish unit and e2e tests for ingest pipeline and schedule a reliability test run against last 90 days of benchmark data
Complete UI accessibility pass and add filter by quantization profile and kernel family
Hook Sentry and runtime traces to the compare UI so triagers can open linked traces in context
Prepare runbook and short training session for oncall (30m) and add to rotation checklist
